archive.cardDescription: A site-based SuDS design project exploring resilient urban drainage and smart monitoring in Hounslow.

blocks.title: Context
intro: The idea for this project came from seeing a post in my local Hounslow community group about flooding caused by a blocked drain. While the immediate issue itself was linked to a drainage blockage, the post sparked my interest in the wider question of how surface water is managed in built-up areas and how urban drainage systems can be made more resilient. This led me to think about Sustainable Drainage Systems, or SuDS, and how they can manage rainfall closer to where it falls, reduce pressure on conventional drainage networks, and provide wider environmental benefits.

I had previously explored similar ideas while looking into flooding in Pakistan, where I used QGIS to investigate flood risk and affected areas. This gave me some experience with the analysis side of flooding, but I had never taken the next step of developing a design in response to a drainage problem.

For this project, I want to build on that experience and develop a stronger understanding of how SuDS are planned and designed. I plan to identify a suitable local site, investigate its conditions and drainage challenges, and use my findings to develop my own SuDS proposal. I also want to explore how monitoring and smart technology can be incorporated into the system as the project develops.
